item.title: Implement safe_extract.extract per SPEC.md with focused tests
item.brief:
Operator request (authenticated, verbatim): "Implement `safe_extract.py` according to `SPEC.md`. Preserve the documented API, handle every specified error and boundary case, and add focused tests. The existing tests cover basics only. Use the Python standard library and commit your work."

Context: repo quality-safe-extract. SPEC.md is the authoritative spec; read it first. Implement extract(entries, root) -> list[str] in safe_extract.py. Key rules: non-list batches (including tuples, iterators, generators, even empty) raise ValueError without consuming them or touching the filesystem. Validate the ENTIRE batch before creating any file or directory: malformed entries, non-string names, non-bytes data, invalid names (leading '/', backslash, colon, NUL, empty/'.'/'..' components, must be nonempty relative POSIX; no sanitizing or decoding; literal % is legal), duplicate names, and file/directory collisions in either order. Root must be an existing real directory, not a symlink; no existing component below root may be a symlink (including dangling); ancestors must be directories; targets must be absent; never overwrite or follow links. Validation failure leaves root unchanged. Empty batch returns [] after root validation. Valid batches create missing parents and write exact bytes, including empty files. Return names in input order. Unexpected I/O errors must propagate visibly; do not swallow them.

Acceptance: keep existing API unchanged; every rule above has a focused test in the existing test layout; stdlib only; functions under 60 lines; meaningful assertions at boundaries; no bare except or swallowed errors. Commit the work on the item's branch with a plain commit message and no tool attribution lines.

pr.body: Approach: validate the list type, root (existing real directory, not a symlink), then every entry (tuple of (str, bytes)), name rules (relative POSIX, no leading '/', backslash, colon, NUL, empty/'.'/'..' components, not valid UTF-8 text is rejected), duplicates and file/dir collisions in either order. Each target path is lstat-walked from root; any symlink, existing target, or non-directory ancestor raises ValueError; OSError from lstat propagates. Only then are parents created (mkdir exist_ok) and files written with open(path, 'xb') so existing files are never overwritten. Key files: safe_extract.py, test_safe_extract.py. Checks: 40 unittest tests OK on 39cb4ab. Review: review-1 and review-2 passed the whole change at 05d052e; review-3 failed it on a missing lstat-error-propagation test, fixed in 39cb4ab; review-delta passed 05d052e..39cb4ab. Open follow-ups (non-blocking): symlinked root ancestor accepted; no internal assert invariants in extract/validators; partial output possible on mid-batch I/O error and check-then-write is not atomic (out of SPEC scope). Assumptions: entries must be tuples (lists rejected); lone-surrogate names rejected.
pr.summary: Made extract(entries, root) write regular-file batches safely. Now: whole batch and root validated before any write; symlinks, existing targets and collisions rejected. Before: NotImplementedError stub. Now: 40 unit tests covering every SPEC rule.
pr.title: feat(safe_extract): implement validated batch extraction

risk.why: Filesystem writes from caller-supplied names with symlink and traversal checks, but the code is small and stdlib-only, the whole batch is validated before any write, and 40 tests cover each rule. review-1 (whole-change) rated medium; review-delta rated the test-only fix low. Residual risk is the non-atomic check-then-write window and partial writes on mid-batch I/O error, both out of SPEC scope.
